name: Termux Proot / Full Linux
description: When Termux's bionic/busybox isn't enough — using proot-distro for a full Debian/Ubuntu/Alpine user-space.
instructions:
1. If a user asks for a tool that has no Termux package, or a `.deb` that won't install because of glibc errors, use proot-distro. It is the supported escape hatch — bionic/busybox is not a real Linux sysroot.
2. Install: `pkg install proot-distro -y && proot-distro install debian` (or `ubuntu`, `alpine`, `fedora`, `archlinux`).
3. Run inside a single call: `proot-distro login debian -- bash -c "your command here"`. The `-- bash -c "..."` form is the only one that works through run_termux_command because the bridge is a single command line. Avoid `proot-distro login <distro>` with no command — it opens an interactive shell and will hang until timeout.
4. Performance: proot uses ptrace and adds ~10x syscall overhead. Long compile jobs (kernel, chromium, firefox) become impractically slow inside proot. Prefer small, focused commands inside proot over a multi-hour build.
5. Not a security boundary: proot is user-space emulation. It does NOT grant real root. Anything that does `setuid(0)` inside proot still fails. Do not promise "root access" via proot.
6. Termux's own proot vs pkg-side proot: `pkg install proot` is the binary; `pkg install proot-distro` is the wrapper for distro images. They are two different packages. The wrapper is what most users want.
7. Root-on-device alternative: `pkg install tsu -y` (or `tsu` from a community package), then `tsu -c "command"` runs with real root via Magisk/SuperSU. This requires the device to be rooted AND the user to have granted Termux root via the Magisk/SuperSU prompt. Do not assume either.
8. Telling the user: if a task takes more than 10 minutes, say so BEFORE starting. Do not promise "Debian will work" without first confirming the user is on a recent Termux (>= 0.118), which is the F-Droid / GitHub build.
9. Distro size: proot-distro images are 200MB-1GB downloaded on first install. The first `proot-distro install <distro>` should be raised to timeout_seconds=600. Subsequent launches are fast (image is cached).
10. Sharing files with proot: proot-distro bind-mounts Termux's home by default, so files in `$HOME` are visible. `/sdcard/Download` is also visible. Outside those, the filesystem is partitioned.
11. systemd is not available inside proot. Services inside proot-boot would need to be started manually per call. Do not promise a "real Linux server" experience.
